Q: converting TEXT to VARCHAR A:

The documentation can be found here, it is in the reference manual.

https://infocenter.sybase.com/help/topic/com.sybase.infocenter.dc36271.1570/html/blocks/blocks42.htm

Adaptive Server Enterprise -> Reference Manual: Building Blocks -> System and User-Defined Datatypes -> Character Types

In summary, if no length is specified in a column or a variable in a declare statement, the length is 1 character. If varchar is used in a covert statement with no length specified, it is defaulted to 30 characters, as your tests show.

Q: pvl8.control file in PostgreSQL is not present A:

Make sure your PLV8 version is the correct version for your Postgres DB. if youre using PSQL 9.4, then you need the plv8 files for PostgreSQL 9.4

I know for Postgresql 9.5 you can find them here: http://www.postgresonline.com/journal/archives/360-PLV8-binaries-for-PostgreSQL-9.5-windows-both-32-bit-and-64-bit.html

and for Postgres 9.4 you can find them here: http://www.postgresonline.com/journal/archives/341-PLV8-binaries-for-PostgreSQL-9.4-windows-both-32-bit-and-64-bit.html

Q: SQL insert into with Hsqldb Script A:

Please try with HSQLDB's DatabaseManagerSwing (you can double click on the hsqldb.jar to start the database manager). First execute the CREATE TABLE statement, then the INSERT statement, finally the SELECT statement.

It should show the correct results.

If you want to use a script to insert data, use the SqlTool.jar which is available in the HSQLDB distribution zip package. See the guide: http://hsqldb.org/doc/2.0/util-guide/

Q: Godot why does wrapf(..) correctly wrap my ship off the screen but conditionally setting position fails? A:

Since your ship is a RigidBody2D, each frame the physics simulation system moves the ship according to its velocity, so it calculates where the ship should be and moves it. You then change that position when setting it directly. This causes for your ship to be in one place according to its position and another place according to the physics simulation, and that is what causes the flickering you're seeing.

According to the RigidBody2D documentation:

If you need to directly affect the body, prefer _integrate_forces() as it allows you to directly access the physics state.

From within the _integrate_forces() function, you can directly access and modify the state of the physics object and it will correctly update the physics simulation.
